title: Hold a steel plate down with one hand while the other slides a strong magnet off it and sets it well clear
instruction: Hold the steel plate down with one hand, and with the other slide the magnet off the plate's end by its knob and set it down on the table at least 5 cm from the plate, then let go. Do not let it snap back onto the plate.
context: Strong pot and neodymium magnets are common in workshops and fabrication. They are taken off steel by sliding, not prying, and must be set down well clear: one that snaps back onto the steel crushes whatever is in between. A light plate slides along with the magnet, so it is held down while the magnet is slid off.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A loose grey steel plate, 770 g, 22 x 9 cm and 5 mm thick, lying along the left-right line 30 cm forward, from 4 cm right of the centre line to 18 cm left. (2) A loose pot magnet, 80 g: a red cup 3.2 cm across and 8 mm tall, a steel stud 1.2 cm across and 3 cm tall and a dark knob 1.8 cm across on top. It clings to the plate (about 20 N) face down, 30 cm forward and 1 cm right of the centre line, 3 cm from the plate's right end. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Off: the magnet's rim at least 2 cm from the plate. Snapped back: once off, its rim came back within 4 mm of the plate, and then the trial scores 0. Let go: both grippers' fingertip centres (TCPs) at least 3 cm from the magnet. 1.0: the magnet's rim at least 5 cm from the plate and let go, never having snapped back; 0.5: off the plate; 0.25: slid at least 2 cm along the plate at some point; else 0.0. The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with the magnet still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Put the magnet back face down on the plate, 3 cm from its right end, and lay the plate where it was.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the pull is a force the task file puts on the magnet (and back on the plate) each step: 20 N face on, times the share of its face over the plate (it fades off the edge); beside the plate 3 N / (1 + (gap / 8 mm)^3) toward it, the gap from the magnet's rim: 1 N at 1 cm, 0.18 N at 2 cm. Cameras 1280 x 704 (Dream-1 sees 320 x 176).
